results.reason: Identifies the §2.2 automatic renewal for successive five-year periods and the 270/240-day window. It calculates October 3 to November 2, 2026, notes lock-in to June 30, 2032 with escalating commitments, and recommends a protective non-renewal notice before the window closes.
Does not mention the §5.3 30-day objection or removal right, the deemed-acceptance mechanism, or the lapsed September 20, 2026 deadline. It only says the notice's formalities appear compliant.

Explains that §11.1 has no fault qualifier and covers Brightmere-caused claims, that §12.3(a) leaves it uncapped, and that §11.2 stays capped. It recommends narrowing §11.1 to Halvorsen's own fault and making the indemnities mutual or capped.

Identifies that First Amendment §3 deletes and replaces §12.3 and drops the recall carve-out. It explains that recall reimbursement is now subject to the 12-month fees cap, which a large recall could exceed, and recommends reinstating the carve-out.

Identifies Delaware law and Wilmington exclusive jurisdiction under First Amendment §6.1–6.2. It contrasts this with New York law and New York County courts in D1 §17.1–17.2, notes the amendment prevails under §1.4, and recommends restoring New York.
The documents table states 'Courier delivery August 21, 2026' for D3.
States that the Initial Term ends June 30, 2027.
States that under D1 §1.4 written amendments prevail over the body of the Agreement.
Formatted as a memorandum to the Supervising Partner. Each issue has 'Where', 'Why it matters for Halvorsen' and 'Recommended fix' sections.
Concludes that recall reimbursement is now capped.
Expressly acknowledges that the Delaware provisions now govern.
